name: Yijing returns from his Indian Ocean pilgrimage
summary: Tang Buddhist monk Yijing (635–713) completes a 24-year journey to India by the southern sea route via Srivijaya (Sumatra), in contrast to Xuanzang's overland route. Spends a decade at Nalanda; returns with 400 Sanskrit texts via Srivijaya, where he writes his record of Mahayana monastic discipline in the Indian Ocean world.

_quarry.structural_significance: Documents the central importance of Srivijaya (Palembang) as the Buddhist learning hub of the maritime Silk Road in the late 7th century; first systematic Chinese-language account of monastic life in late-Gupta-successor India.
